items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, the decision block and c1 make the hold clear, give the reason (the two configurations that hold 97% in every task have overall p95s of 870 ms and 2551 ms) and name the main risk. But the lede and the Recommendation say a budget at or above 870 ms 'would change the answer'. The overall p95 is only the lowest such a budget could be. The latency gate applies within each task, so at least one task's p95 for Brisk-S · reasoning high · 1 retry must be at or above 870 ms. A latency owner who moves the budget to 870 ms would not be enough to qualify it.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: I checked each claim row by row against its block and the appendix. c1 holds: only Atlas-M · high · retry (97.9%) and Brisk-S · high · retry (97.3%) pass multi-hop, and every other configuration misses there. c2 holds: J at 513 ms, I at 465 ms and S at 450 ms are under 600 ms, and each misses some task. c3's gaps (95.6%, 96.4%, 97.0%) and c4's 5.5× ($3.477 vs $0.633) match the data. Nothing contradicts the headline.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: L's thin clearances are shown, with wrong-side odds of 37.4%, 29.9% and 16.5%, which I confirmed. But the hold also depends on the closest configuration under the budget, Brisk-S · low · retry, really missing the gate, and that is framed more firmly than the data allow. The per-task clause says its 1.4-point multi-hop miss means 'the hold does not rest on' the counts. Assuming each task got its traffic share of cases, that miss reads on the wrong side 11.9% of the time, the 0.6-point ambiguous-entity miss 33.3%, and date math sits on the line at 50%. None of J's margins appear in Watch.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Nothing omitted would change the decision. Nano-XS misses in every task; overall pass rate, calls per task and p50 latency are not gated; and the snapshot holds no figures for extra calls or outcome.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The overall-only latency reading is handled well: if the tasks split the cases, the overall p95 above 600 ms forces at least one task over 600 ms. The unnamed provider is not handled where it matters. Method says the routing behind the costs is unknown, but c4 and the 'Why not the others' line give the 5.5× ratio and $11,376 a month as if they belonged to the models.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an action and what it would settle: per-task p95, a declaration on the budget, a fix-and-rerun on the two weak tasks, and a 22,911-case confirmation, which I checked against the two-sided 80% size. The second step's '870 ms' target inherits the problem in item 1.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: c3's claim is about gaps (1.4 points, 0.6, exactly on the line), but its block shows only three failure examples, so none of those figures is drawn. c2's second half (every configuration under the budget misses the pass rate somewhere) is not drawn in its latency block either. c1's heatmap and c4's bars and interval do fit their claims.

findings.finding: c4, its caption and the decision's 'costs 5.5 times as much' line compare costs ($3.48 vs $0.63 per 1,000 calls, $11,376 a month) with no provider named for either model. The snapshot does not say who served Atlas-M or Brisk-S, and only Method mentions that. Fix: say in the c4 sentence and in the decision line that no provider is named for either configuration, so the 5.5× ratio and the monthly gap reflect this run's unnamed routing and may not hold under another one.

The lede ('A budget at or above that p95… would change the answer') and the second next step ('could rise to 870 ms') treat 870 ms as enough for Brisk-S · reasoning high · 1 retry. The page's own argument in the latency clause shows the opposite. The gate applies within each task, and if the tasks split the cases, at least one task's p95 must be at or above the overall 870 ms. Multi-hop, with 2 to 3 calls, is likely slower still. Fix: say the budget would need to cover L's slowest task's p95, which is at least 870 ms and has not been read. Make the per-task latency read the first thing that would change the answer, and phrase the budget declaration as 'at least 870 ms, exact level pending the per-task read'.

Confidence and Watch understate the risk on the side of the hold that could flip it toward a ship. The per-task-counts clause says configurations under the budget miss 'by at least 1.4 points somewhere, so the hold does not rest on them'. Assuming each task got its traffic share of cases, Brisk-S · low · retry's 1.4-point multi-hop miss reads on the wrong side 11.9% of the time, its 0.6-point ambiguous-entity miss 33.3%, and its date math is on the line. Fix: quote the 11.9% in that clause and add J's multi-hop and ambiguous-entity margins to Watch, since a rerun there is what could turn the hold into a pick. Separately, the best-of-n clause says a lower re-read of L would 'leave no configuration holding the pass rate everywhere'. That is wrong, because Atlas-M · high · retry clears multi-hop by 0.9 points and ambiguous entities by 1.3. Say 'would leave only Atlas-M · high · retry holding'.

c3's sentence rests on J's per-task gaps (multi-hop 95.6%, ambiguous entity 96.4%, date math 97.0% against 97%), but its block holds only three failure examples, so the claim's own figures are not drawn. c2's second half (every configuration under the budget misses somewhere) has the same problem. Fix: give c3 a block showing per-task pass rates against the 97% line for the configurations under the budget (J, I, S), and keep the examples as a second block. Also fix the examples caption: it says 'one per task where it struggles', but J holds date math at exactly 97.0%. It also lists the examples in the order first, third, second, and does not say how many failures each was kept from.

The $11,376-a-month gap prices the 4,000,000 monthly volume as calls. Method says the volume's unit is not stated, and these configurations make about 1.45 calls per task. If the volume counts tasks, the gap is about 45% larger. Say in the caption that the monthly gap assumes the volume counts calls. A smaller point: the dot reads -0.7 while the options table's rounded rates (98.0% vs 98.6%) suggest -0.6. Add a note that the difference is computed before rounding.

And its overall p95 is 513 ms, so its slowest task is at least that slow and has not been read against 600 ms. Fix: add date-math cases to the rerun, and change the outcome to 'becomes the pick only if date math also holds and its per-task p95 stays under 600 ms'. Match the confidence clause's 'pending per-task latency' wording.
